Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:26134

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Jabalpur
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Himanshu Joshi

On The 23rd Of March, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 17331 of 2023
 Deepak
 Versus
 The State Of M.P.
 Appearance:
 Dr. Anuvad Shrivastava - Advocate for the applicant.
 Smt. Chetna Gupta - Pl for the respondent/State .
 Order

This petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed seeking quashment of order dated 21.03.2023 passed by the 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Sagar in Criminal Revision No. 61/2023, whereby the order dated 05.04.2018 passed by JMFC, Sagar in Criminal Case No.2192/2014 has been affirmed, rejecting the applicant's prayer for discharge and for prosecuting the nominee of the company under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

2. The relevant facts are that a complaint was filed under Section 26(2)(1) read with Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 against one Virendra Kumar Jain, proprietor of "Virendra Pan Masala", alleging sale of sub-standard pan masala.
3. Initially, the present applicant was not arraigned as an accused in the case.
Subsequently, an application under Section 319 of the Code of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26134 2 MCRC-17331-2023 Criminal Procedure was filed seeking to implead the applicant as an accused.

entities.text: Code of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26134 2 MCRC-17331-2023 Criminal Procedure
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The said application was rejected by the Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) vide order dated 19.02.2015.
However, in revision, the said order was set aside and the application was allowed on 27.08.2015.
The said order was further affirmed by the High Court on 06.07.2017 in Criminal Revision No. 2642/2015, pursuant to which the applicant came to be added as an accused in the case.

4. The applicant thereafter filed an application (Annexure A/5) before the trial Court seeking discharge, and prosecution of the nominated person (Mr. Pankaj P.Wala), appointed by Board Resolution dated 05.03.2012 under Section 66 of the Act.

sentences.text: The JMFC, by order dated 05.04.2018, rejected the application.

A revision petition filed against the said order was subsequently dismissed by the Sessions Court on 21.03.2023, primarily on the ground that the High Court had already granted permission to prosecute the applicant.
Hence, the present petition.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that Section 66 of the Act provides a statutory mechanism for nomination, and liability must fall on the nominated person.
The company had already nominated a responsible person for food safety compliance.
The applicant is merely a Director and not in charge of day-to-day operations.
The Courts below failed to appreciate the statutory scheme and wrongly rejected the application.
Continuation of proceedings against the applicant amounts to abuse of process of law.

7. Learned counsel for the State/respondent submits that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:26134 3 MCRC-17331-2023 applicant has already been impleaded as an accused pursuant to earlier orders upheld by the High Court.
The issue of liability cannot be adjudicated at this stage.
The nomination does not automatically absolve other responsible persons.
Thus, the matter requires trial.
8. The applicant relies upon nomination of Mr. Pankaj P. Wala.
However, Section 66 provides for fixing responsibility, not automatic exoneration.

The proviso indicates liability of "person in-charge"
of the unit.
At this stage whether the nominee was actually responsible or the applicant had any role or knowledge are questions of fact, requiring evidence.

9. Section 66 of the Food Safety and Standards Act. 2006 provides that where an offence is committed by a company the persons in charge are liable, and the company may nominate a responsible person for a unit/branch.
However, nomination does not automatically exclude liability of other persons.
Liability depends on role, responsibility, knowledge or negligence.
10. It is an admitted position that the applicant has already been impleaded as an accused.
Such impleadment was upheld by the High Court in earlier proceedings.
Thus, the issue of summoning has attained finality and the present petition cannot indirectly challenge the same.
11. The inherent power can be exercised to prevent abuse of process of Court or to secure ends of justice.
At this stage, the Court cannot conduct a mini-trial
The defence of nomination is to be tested during trial.
12. This Court is of the considered view that the applicant has already been validly arraigned as an accused and the plea based on nomination involves disputed questions of fact.
No ground for quashing or NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26134 4 MCRC-17331-2023 discharge under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is made out.
13. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
The impugned orders dated 05.04.2018 and 21.03.2023 are hereby affirmed.
The trial Court shall proceed with the matter in accordance with law.

It is clarified that the applicant is at liberty to raise all permissible defences, including the plea of Deepak vs The State Of M.P. on 23 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81749476/
